800776382171.title: SKER Sweden metal/enamal White/Blue Rim Cup/saucer 7&12cm Set, stamped c1930-50
800776382171.desc: Kockums Emaljverk, Ronneby, Sweden — white and cobalt-blue vitreous enamel coffee/demitasse cup and saucer, 7 cm cup / 12 cm saucer, KER seal, circa 1930s–1950s. ***chip on bottom of the cup, no rust there or at the handle attachment site**** This is marked 7 cm and the saucer 12 cm, with the same blue Kockums/KER Sweden seal. That strongly supports them being an original matched Kockums cup-and-saucer service rather than two generic Swedish enamel pieces. The white enamel with dark blue edging is also historically correct for Kockums. A Swedish museum describes Kockums white enamel with blue trim, noting that this blue-and-white enamelware was produced from the late 19th century onward. Kockums’ best-known later color scheme, the cream body with green trim called Cream Lux, was introduced in 1935. Your white/blue set belongs to the older traditional Kockums color family rather than Cream Lux. Dating this particular set The mark style is the useful clue. Period Kockums advertising signs using “Kockums Emalj Sweden – KER” are documented to the 1940s–1950s, and surviving Kockums pieces carrying closely related KER/seal marks are routinely associated with that era. Based on the combination of: KER seal + SWEDEN + metric size + white/blue enamel + cup-and-saucer form I would currently date yours most plausibly to about 1930s–1950s, with 1940s–early 1950s being a very reasonable working estimate. And this isn’t merely seller attribution: a 1947 Swedish industrial directory lists Kockums Emaljerverk, Ronneby as an operating enamel manufacturer, giving us contemporary documentary confirmation of the company during exactly this period.

ABOUT THE ARTIST Jack Coughlin (1932–2025) was an accomplished American artist and master printmaker particularly recognized for his expressive portraits of important writers, artists and cultural figures. He taught drawing and printmaking at the University of Massachusetts Amherst for approximately 35 years and later became Professor Emeritus. Coughlin was elected to the National Academy of Design in 1972, and his work is represented in major institutional collections, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, National Gallery of Art and Smithsonian American Art Museum, among others. ABOUT THE SUBJECT Eugene O’Neill (1888–1953) is regarded as one of the most important American playwrights of the 20th century. He was the first American playwright awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, receiving the honor in 1936, and won four Pulitzer Prizes for Drama. His celebrated works include Long Day’s Journey Into Night, The Iceman Cometh, Anna Christie and Beyond the Horizon. Coughlin became particularly associated with portraits of literary figures, making this limited-edition O’Neill portrait a particularly fitting example of his body of work. 206614725018.title: Antique c1870 Amand-Durand Albrecht Durer Christ Before Pilate Heliogravure

The lower margin is printed “Héliogrᵉ et imp. A. Durand - Paris,” identifying the work as a heliogravure printed by Charles Amand-Durand (1831-1905) in Paris. Amand-Durand became known in the 19th century for producing highly detailed heliogravure reproductions of important Old Master prints. Cataloged examples of this particular Dürer composition date to approximately 1870 . The original composition was engraved by Albrecht Dürer in 1512 as part of his Engraved Passion . This is a 19th-century Amand-Durand reproduction after Dürer , not an original 1512 Dürer impression. There is an old pencil identification inscription in the lower margin. 287638057167.title: Set of Four Vintage Press-Back Oak Dining Chairs
287638057167.desc: This set of four vintage dining chairs manufactured by Shin-Lee, a well-known Taiwanese furniture maker active during the late 20th century. Constructed from solid oak with a warm golden oak finish, each chair displays prominent grain patterns characteristic of crown-cut timber. The backrests are the focal point, featuring deep-relief machine-pressed floral and scrollwork motifs on the top rail and central splat, mimicking the hand-carving of earlier eras. The splats are urn-shaped with elegant curves, flanked by turned stiles that terminate in small decorative finials. The seats are contoured for comfort, made of solid wood planks with rounded edges. The undercarriage consists of four turned legs supported by double side-stretchers and a single front-stretcher with decorative bulbous turning. While generally in good structural condition, visible signs of age include light surface scratches on the seats, minor finish wear on the stretcher rails where feet would rest, and a slight patina consistent with four decades of light household use. A defining feature is information provided by a silver metallic rectangular foil label with black typeface that reads '84 $ Shin-Lee'. This indicates a manufacture or copyright date of 1984. The label is adhered directly to the wood surface, showing minor lifting at the right edge and some light scratching, suggesting it is original to the piece. Shin-Lee is particularly recognized for producing high-quality Windsor-style chairs, rocking chairs, and dining sets for the international market, specifically following Early American or Colonial Revival aesthetics popular in the early 1980s. The craftsmanship displays a focus on mass-production durability, utilizing machine-milled components with a standardized finish application. Free local delivery within 100 miles of Lebanon Oregon. Buyer may arrange for shipping at their expense.

287638057591.title: Late Victorian Golden Oak Rocking Chair with Pressed Back and Caned Seat
287638057591.desc: This is a fine example of a Late Victorian to Edwardian era (circa 1890-1910) 'pressed back' rocking chair, constructed primarily from solid quartersawn white oak with a characteristic golden honey finish. The chair features a high back with a decorative top crest and three horizontal splats. The most prominent feature is the ornate mechanical wood-pressing technique used on the crest and center splats, mimicking hand-carving with intricate scrolling acanthus leaves, foliate patterns, and stylized floral motifs. The frame displays classic turn-of-the-century craftsmanship with spindle turnings on the uprights and a four-spindle support structure between the middle splats. The seat is an inset natural cane panel in a traditional octagonal weave pattern, showing minor sagging consistent with age but remaining mostly intact. The wood demonstrates a rich patina with visible graining (medullary rays) typical of high-quality oak furniture from this period. Notable condition observations include minor surface abrasions, localized darkening of the finish in high-touch areas, and some visible hardware fasteners (pins/screws) on the inner stiles which appear to be original production methods of the time. This style was a staple of American middle-class parlors and is often associated with the 'Larkin' era of production furniture. ***Note in photos that the two outside spindles are missing, but the holes are plugged. Free local delivery within 75miles of Lebanon, Oregon

820221614649.title: 2 Victorian Harrach Bohemian Pink Satin Glass Bud Vases, Hand-Numbered 8/7
820221614649.desc: These exceptional vases are fine examples of late 19th-century Bohemian art glass from the renowned Harrach glassworks. Identified by the hand-inked pattern numbers "8/7" on the base, this set was produced during the height of the Victorian Art Glass movement (circa 1890). ​Unlike mass-produced mid-century pieces, these feature a sophisticated acid-etched "satin" finish over a cased opal glass body. The hand-painted gold gilt highlights were applied by professional factory gilders, a detail confirmed by the matching decorator's marks. This is a rare opportunity to own a verified, matching pair from a single production batch. The handwritten fractional mark (8/7) is the strongest evidence for Harrach. Unlike American makers (Fenton, Mt. Washington) who used molded marks or paper labels, Bohemian factories utilized a system of hand-inked pattern and decorator numbers on the polished pontil or base. - ​Pattern 8/7: In Bohemian glass catalogs, these numbers correspond to specific shapes and decoration styles used for export to the English and American markets between 1885 and 1900. - ​The Style: This specific shade of "Peachblow" (pink-to-white casing) with gold gilt banding was a signature Harrach export. While often sold under the generic name "Bristol Glass" in the UK and US, the quality and numerical coding point directly to the St. Stephens-Wald region. Design Highlights: - ​Color: A soft, glowing "blush" pink that transitions beautifully in natural light. - ​Gilding: Features hand-applied gold gilt bands on the neck and rim, showing the delicate craftsmanship of the period. - ​Condition: Both pieces are in exceptional antique condition. The presence of both vases from the original set is rare, as these were often separated over the last 140 years. Shipping cost includes insurance.
